root.claim: There is one deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes that computes the exact $2n$-bit product of two $n$-bit integers for every $n\ge1$ in worst-case time $T_A(n)=O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$; hence $n\log n$ is not the optimal order of multiplication cost in this model, contrary to the Schonhage-Strassen conjecture.
root.method: Reduce multiplication to a radix-digit convolution computed by approximate Fourier transforms over the polynomial ring $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$; accelerate the two operations that would each cost $\Theta(n\log n)$, address rearrangement and butterfly layers, by recursive procedures built from fixed linear networks with a rank saving $s<Wm$; then verify exact recovery of the integer coefficients and sum a cost table whose every term is a power of $\log n$ strictly below one.

motivation.text: In the transform representation the work consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts and butterflies; since even scanning the array once per transform level already costs $n\log n$, both the data movement and the arithmetic layers must be made sublinear per level, which the two network-based procedures achieve.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$. We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

children.claim: A fixed linear network with $W$ wires, labelled by subspaces of an $m$-dimensional space so that the edge changes need $s<Wm$ smaller calls in total, turns one call at parameter $e=m^k$ on logical volume $V$ into $s$ calls at parameter $e/m$ on role streams of volume $V/W$; the resulting recurrence $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$ for cost per unit volume has solution $F_k=O(e^\tau)$ with $\tau=1-2^{-50}<1$, and in particular two address chunks of $m^k$ digits are interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time.
children.method: Build a scalar three-stage bank exchange that restores its scratch wires; lift scalars to arrays with a frame at each vertex so that only endpoint operators remain on every role; attach nested subspace labels built from three-element subsets so that the total residual dimension is $Wm-2N+2L$ with $L<N/2$; implement each unit of an edge's rank by one smaller interchange after a triangular factorization; split rows among the $W$ roles so each smaller call has volume $V/W$ and solve the recurrence by a geometric sum.

motivation.text: Dividing cost by volume, a call at parameter $mf$ contributes $s/W$ times the normalized cost at parameter $f$; because $s/W<m$ this contribution grows more slowly than the parameter, which is exactly a power saving, and the sources name this strict inequality as the source of the saving.

quote.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial values of its auxiliary wires, the eight-row forward schedule changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and nothing else, and the three stages (forward, inverse forward with the banks exchanged, forward) send $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$ while restoring every auxiliary value; over $\mathbb F_2$ this is the permutation exchanging $X_a$ and $Y_a$.
children.method: Write the schedule as: subtract the effect of the old scratch values, copy and gather the sources, scatter and side-inject into the targets, undo gather and copy; compute the net target change as a linear map independent of the initial scratch values, and evaluate its coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ by the intersection size $|S\cap T|$.

motivation.text: Scratch wires start with arbitrary contents, so the schedule first subtracts whatever effect those contents would have on the targets, then adds the source contribution, then undoes its own changes to the scratch wires; this is the linear form of the transparent-computation restoration of Buhrman, Cleve, Koucky, Loff and Speelman.

quote.quote: The first two rows of the following schedule remove the effect of the old scratch values; the next four introduce the source values and add their effect to the target; the last two restore the scratch values.

children.claim: The net change of the target bank is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independent of the initial side and central values $a,c$: rows 0 and 1 subtract $\mathcal Ja+\mathcal Rc$, rows 2 and 3 change the scratch values to $a+\mathcal Vx$ and $c+\mathcal Gx$, rows 4 and 5 add $\mathcal R(c+\mathcal Gx)+\mathcal J(a+\mathcal Vx)$, and rows 6 and 7 restore $c,a$.

quote.quote: If the initial side and central vectors are $a,c$, the first two rows subtract $\mathcal J a+\mathcal R c$ from $y$. Rows 2 and 3 change them to $a+\mathcal Vx,c+\mathcal Gx$. Rows 4 and 5 therefore add $\mathcal R(c+\mathcal Gx)+\mathcal J(a+\mathcal Vx)$. Rows 6 and 7 restore $c,a$. The net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of $a,c$.

children.claim: The central coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$ in the bit case and $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$ in the complex case; the side wires cancel exactly the neighboring cases ($|S\cap T|=1$ for bits, $|S\cap T|\in\{0,2\}$ for the complex network), the remaining distinct triples already have coefficient zero, and the self coefficient is one, so both net maps are $y\leftarrow y+x$.

quote.quote: In the bit case, the central coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$. The side contribution cancels exactly the intersection-one cases; distinct triples with intersection zero or two already have coefficient zero, and the self coefficient is one. In the complex case, the central coefficient is $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$. The side cancels it for distinct triples with intersection zero or two; intersection one contributes zero, and the self coefficient is one. Thus both net maps are $y\gets y+x$.

children.claim: The inverse schedule with logical source $Y$ and target $X$ effects $X\leftarrow X-Y$, so the three stages take $(x,y)$ to $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$, and each invocation restores its own auxiliary wires.

quote.quote: The inverse schedule with logical source $Y$ and target $X$ effects $X\gets X-Y$. Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$. Each invocation restores its own auxiliary wires.

children.salient: Auxiliary wires may start with arbitrary values and are returned to them exactly, so when rows of a real array are later assigned to scratch roles no initialization is needed.

adds.name: data banks
adds.meaning: the two banks of data wires, indexed by triples of triples $a\in\mathcal T^3$

adds.name: source value
adds.meaning: the control value of the source wire whose varying triple is $T$

adds.name: target value
adds.meaning: the value updated on the target wire whose varying triple is $S$

children.claim: Replacing each scalar by an array in $R^\Omega$ and assigning an invertible frame $D_v$ at each source, gate and sink, with the edge from $u$ to $v$ applying $D_vD_u^{-1}$ and the input interpreted as $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$, the network implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$; when the scalar network is a signed role permutation $\rho$, the route from role $w$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$, on every role including the auxiliary ones.
children.method: Maintain the invariant that the stored array at a vertex equals $D_v$ applied to the logical array there, using $R$-linearity so that a common frame commutes with each pointwise gate; then telescope the frames along each route.

motivation.text: Because the frames cancel across every gate, the operator a role receives depends only on its source and sink frames, which leaves the intermediate frames free to be chosen so that every edge change is cheap.

quote.quote: Once the scalar routing is fixed, the endpoint frames determine the array operator on each route; the intermediate frames can then be chosen to make each edge change inexpensive.

children.claim: At a vertex $v$ the stored array is $D_v$ applied to the logical array: on an edge with logical array $\varphi$ the operator changes $D_u\varphi$ to $D_v\varphi$, and at a gate $R$-linearity gives $\sum_jc_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_jc_j\varphi_j)$, so the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate and the invariant continues to the sinks.

quote.quote: At a vertex $v$, the invariant is that the stored array equals $D_v$ applied to the logical array there. It holds at the sources by definition. On an edge whose logical array is $\varphi$, the edge operator changes $D_u\varphi$ to $D_v\varphi$. At a gate with logical input arrays $\varphi_j$, $R$-linearity gives $\sum_j c_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_j c_j\varphi_j)$ for each output combination, with $c_j\in R$. Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.claim: The implemented operator is $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$; if the scalar network sends input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w$, that route applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its input array, and all roles, including auxiliary roles, enter this identity.

quote.quote: In particular, if the scalar network is a signed role permutation that sends input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with scalar sign $\varepsilon_w$, that route applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))} D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its input array. All roles, including the auxiliary roles, enter this identity. Once the scalar routing is fixed, the endpoint frames determine the array operator on each route; the intermediate frames can then be chosen to make each edge change inexpensive.

adds.name: frame
adds.meaning: the invertible linear operator on arrays assigned to vertex $v$, so that the stored array is $D_v$ applied to the logical array

adds.name: role permutation
adds.meaning: the permutation of roles induced by the scalar network, exchanging $X_a$ and $Y_a$ and fixing scratch roles

adds.name: array network
adds.meaning: the scalar network applied pointwise at every address of the common address set $\Omega$

children.claim: Nondegenerate subspace labels of the $m$-dimensional space $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$, built from indicator vectors of triples, can be attached to every source, gate and sink so that every edge joins comparable labels, the only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4 with loss $h$, and the sum of absolute dimension changes is $Wm-2N+2L$ with $L=Ich<N/2$; hence the edge rank sums are $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$ and $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$, and $s/W<m^\tau$ for $\tau=1-2^{-50}$.
children.method: Use the bilinear form $\langle x,y\rangle=x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$ on $\mathbb Q^h$ (the dot product on $\mathbb F_2^h$ for the complex network) so that neighboring triple lines are orthogonal; prescribe terminal labels $U_a$, $\mathcal F$ on $X_a$, $0$, $U_a^\perp$ on $Y_a$ and $0$, $\mathcal F$ on scratch roles; expose one tensor factor per stage; tabulate the orthogonal residual of every edge; telescope the signed dimension changes at gates and count the decreasing edges.

motivation.text: Each unit of residual dimension on an edge costs one smaller call, and the terminal labels force the signed total to be $Wm-2N$, so the saving must come from keeping the dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to $N$.

quote.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space. On every edge one label will contain the other. For such an edge, the \emph{orthogonal residual} is the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one; its dimension is the absolute change in label dimension. The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to $N$.

children.claim: With $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$ and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$ over $\mathbb Q$, and $t_T\cdot t_T=1$ for the dot product over $\mathbb F_2$, every triple line is nondegenerate and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal in the label field of either construction.

quote.quote: \langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1, \qquad \langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2. \] For the complex network, take instead $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ with the ordinary dot product; here $t_T\cdot t_T=1$. Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction. The scalar domain need not equal the label field.

children.claim: The source label dimensions sum to $N$ and the sink dimensions to $Wm-N$, so the signed dimension changes sum to $Wm-2N$ because contributions at gates cancel; if decreasing edges lose a total dimension $L$, the absolute changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$, and $L<N/2$ leaves a strict saving even after the rational interface adds $N$ source ranks.

quote.quote: Write $W$ for the wire count in the construction under consideration. The source dimensions sum to $N$ and the sink dimensions to $Wm-N$. Thus the signed dimension changes will sum to $Wm-2N$, because the contributions at gates cancel. If decreasing edges lose a total dimension $L$, the sum of absolute changes is $Wm-2N+2L$. We will obtain $L<N/2$. The rational interface below will require an additional $N$ source ranks, so this inequality will leave a strict saving in both constructions.

children.claim: The stage transitions $X\colon A\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q\to(A\otimes F)\otimes Q$ and $Y\colon B\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q\to((B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t^\perp))\otimes Q$ fit together: the outgoing labels are exactly the next stage's incoming labels, starting at $U_a$ on $X_a$ and $0$ on $Y_a$ and ending at $\mathcal F$ and $U_a^\perp$ as prescribed at the terminals.

quote.quote: Thus the prescribed outgoing labels are $A'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes Q'$ on $X$ and $B'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes Q'$ on $Y$, exactly the next incoming labels. At stage 1 they start at $U_a$ on $X_a$ and zero on $Y_a$; at stage 3 they end at $\mathcal F$ on $X_a$ and $U_a^\perp$ on $Y_a$, as prescribed at the terminals.

children.claim: In the residual table, label dimension is nondecreasing along every edge except center $3\to4$, which removes $P\otimes F\otimes Q$ of dimension $h$; the signed sum telescopes at every gate because each touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence with the same gate label, so it equals $Wm-2N$, and the $Ic$ decreasing edges of loss $h$ add $2L$ with $L=Ich$ when signed changes are replaced by absolute ones.

quote.quote: Label dimension is nondecreasing along every edge except center $3\to4$, which removes $P\otimes F\otimes Q$. The table includes the interstage edges through $\mathrm{in}$, and the initial and final data labels match their terminals, so no other dimension changes occur. The signed sum of dimension changes telescopes at every gate: each touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence with the same gate label. The sum of source dimensions is $N$, while the sum of sink dimensions is $Wm-N$. The signed increase is therefore $Wm-2N$. There are $Ic$ decreasing edges, each of loss $h$; replacing signed changes by absolute changes adds $2L$.

children.claim: The loss ratios are exactly $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$, both smaller than $1/2$ (and over $\mathbb F_2$ every nonzero residual contains a norm-one vector, hence has an orthonormal basis).

quote.quote: The loss ratios have the exact values \[ \frac{L_{\rm b}}{N}=\frac{100}{539},\qquad \frac{L_{\rm c}}{N}=\frac{101}{539}. \] In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.claim: Assigning the projection $P_U$ to each gate or sink with label $U$ and $-P_{U_a}$ to source $X_a$, the rank of an edge difference $P_V-P_U$ with $U\subset V$ equals $\dim V-\dim U$; the only exceptions are the $N$ negative source projections, whose first edge matrix $2P_{U_a}$ has rank one where the dimension change is zero, so $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}$ with deficit $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$, and the endpoint difference is $I_m$ on every role.

quote.quote: Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar-motifs} gives the scalar permutation, including all auxiliary roles. For $U\subset V$ nondegenerate, $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its orthogonal complement. Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$; reversing the edge negates the matrix without changing its rank. The only exceptions are the $N$ negative source projections. At stage 1, $B=0$, and the first gate on $X_a$ has label exactly $U_a$. Its first edge matrix is therefore $2P_{U_a}$, of rational rank one, where the corresponding dimension change was zero. Lemma~\ref{lem:motif-residuals} consequently gives the stated rank sum. Its deficit from $W_{\rm b}m$ is $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$. For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$. Every other role has zero source matrix and identity sink matrix. This proves the interface.

children.claim: For the complex network with binary labels and frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$, each edge's frame change $\mathcal C_V\mathcal C_U^{-1}$ is a product of one translation kernel $aI+bX_v$, or its inverse, per vector of an orthonormal basis of the residual; the number of factors sums to $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$, and after endpoint corrections every role receives $C^{\otimes m}$.

quote.quote: For each edge of the complex network, write $U,V$ for its tail and head labels. Its phase-frame difference $\mathcal C_V\mathcal C_U^{-1}$ is a product of one translation kernel $aI+bX_v$, or its inverse, per vector in an orthonormal basis of the edge residual. Here $(X_vf)(x)=f(x+v)$. The sum of these basis lengths is \[ s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c} =1873807244636671267308000000<W_{\rm c}m. \] After source and sink diagonal corrections, and undoing the signed bank exchange, telescoping these phase frames gives $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role, including auxiliary roles. The same assertion holds on any positive number of columns by taking tensor products over columns.

children.claim: The relative deficits $\eta_{\rm b}=339/22587335000000$ and $\eta_{\rm c}=73/19906842167500$ both exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}$; since $m<2^{20}$, $m^{1-2^{-50}}=m\exp(-2^{-50}\log m)>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta)$, so $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$. Since $m<2^{20}$ and $\log 2<1$, we have $\log m<20$, whence \[ m^{1-2^{-50}} =m\exp(-2^{-50}\log m) >m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta) \] for either $\eta=\eta_{\rm b}$ or $\eta=\eta_{\rm c}$. Consequently \[ \frac{s_{\rm b}}{W_{\rm b}}<m^\tau, \qquad \frac{s_{\rm c}}{W_{\rm c}}<m^\sigma, \qquad 0<\tau=\sigma<1.

children.salient: Although the label dimensions must climb from a total of $N$ at the sources to $Wm-N$ at the sinks, the only edges that ever lose dimension are the central-wire returns, each losing exactly $h$, so the loss ratio $L/N$ is the fixed number $100/539$ or $101/539$ independent of everything else.

adds.meaning: the tensor cube $F^{\otimes3}$ of the triple space, of dimension $m$, whose subspaces label vertices

adds.name: triple indicator
adds.meaning: the indicator vector in $F$ of the three-element subset $T$

adds.name: data line
adds.meaning: the line spanned by $u_a=t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}$, the source label of $X_a$

adds.name: earlier stage space
adds.meaning: the tensor space $F^{\otimes(j-1)}$ of the stages before stage $j$

adds.name: earlier stage line
adds.meaning: the line spanned by the tensor of the earlier triple indicators inside $A$

adds.name: earlier complement
adds.meaning: the orthogonal complement $P^\perp$ of $P$ inside $A$

adds.name: later stage line
adds.meaning: the line spanned by the tensor of the later triple indicators

adds.name: projection
adds.meaning: the projection onto the nondegenerate subspace $U$ along $U^\perp$, the rational matrix at a vertex with label $U$

adds.name: phase frame
adds.meaning: the binary-label frame $H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$ of the complex network

adds.name: relative deficit
adds.meaning: the fraction $(Wm-s)/(Wm)$ by which the rank sum falls short of $Wm$

adds.name: complex exponent
adds.meaning: the rational exponent with $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$, equal to $\tau$

children.claim: For two groups $H=(H_1,\ldots,H_m)$ and $D=(D_1,\ldots,D_m)$ of fields over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ with every $H_i$ before every $D_j$, and a fixed rational matrix $A$ of rank $a$, the address shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit fields, each between an $H$ field and a $D$ field, plus $O(V)$ further work.
children.method: Factor $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with invertible lower triangular rational $E_1,E_2$ and a partial permutation $\Pi$ with exactly $a$ ones; perform the triangular changes of coordinates by controlled shifts in descending coordinate order, modulo a fixed odd prime power avoiding all denominators; realize each one of $\Pi$ by two controlled additions around one field interchange.

motivation.text: A controlled shift costs $O(V)$ only when its target field follows its control fields, so a change of coordinates must be lower triangular in tape order; the Bruhat-type factorization isolates all of the rank in a partial permutation, which is the only part that needs interchanges.

quote.quote: Lemma~\ref{lem:ordered-affine-streams} updates a later field using earlier fields in linear time. Lower triangular changes of coordinates can be performed entirely in this direction.

children.claim: If a target field $y\in[Q]$, $Q=q^b$, follows its control fields, the update $y\mapsto y+a(\text{controls})\pmod Q$ costs $O(V)$ whenever the offset is prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time: for each prefix the fiber of $Q$ blocks is split at $Q-a$ and the two pieces are merged in the opposite order, becoming the ranges $[0,a)$ and $[a,Q)$ of the new target coordinate.

quote.quote: Fix all fields before the target, and let the suffix length be $B$ bits. The resulting fiber consists of $Q$ consecutive blocks of length $B$. For an offset $a\in[Q]$, split these blocks at $Q-a$. Append the two pieces to two tapes, doing so successively for all prefix fibers. In the merge read the second piece and then the first piece for each prefix. The pieces have become the two consecutive ranges $[0,a)$ and $[a,Q)$ of the new target coordinate. Recompute $a$ when starting that prefix in the merge. Initializing these two piece lengths and returning the heads of the relevant control counters is included in the $b^{O(1)}$ offset work.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ factors as $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1,E_2$ invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ having exactly $a$ ones, at most one per row and column: choose the topmost nonzero row and its rightmost nonzero entry as pivot, clear with lower triangular elementary matrices on both sides, delete the pivot row and column and repeat, each step isolating a rank-one block.

quote.quote: Delete the pivot row and column from the active index sets, retaining their original orders, and repeat. Elementary operations on the active indices are still lower triangular in the original order. They do not change any earlier pivot row or column, whose other entries have already been cleared. Each step isolates a rank-one block and leaves the remaining rank in the active submatrix. Thus the final partial permutation matrix has exactly $a$ ones. If $LAR=\Pi$ is the resulting identity, then $E_1=L^{-1}$ and $E_2=R^{-1}$ have the required form.

children.claim: Transform $D$ by $E_2$ and $H$ by $E_1^{-1}$, add $\Pi D$ to $H$, then transform $H$ by $E_1$ and $D$ by $E_2^{-1}$; each one at $(i,j)$ of $\Pi$ is $H_i\leftarrow H_i+D_j$, implemented by $D_j\leftarrow D_j+H_i$, $(H_i,D_j)\leftarrow(D_j,H_i)$, $D_j\leftarrow H_i-D_j$, which on $(h,d)$ yields $(h+d,d)$ with one interchange, so the number of recursive calls is the rational rank $a$ and temporary tapes do not multiply it.

quote.quote: For $A=E_1\Pi E_2$, first transform $D$ by $E_2$ and $H$ by $E_1^{-1}$, then add $\Pi D$ to $H$, and finally transform $H$ by $E_1$ and $D$ by $E_2^{-1}$. Each one in position $(i,j)$ of $\Pi$ calls for $H_i\leftarrow H_i+D_j$. Implement it by \[ D_j\leftarrow D_j+H_i,\qquad (H_i,D_j)\leftarrow(D_j,H_i),\qquad D_j\leftarrow H_i-D_j. \] The first and last updates target a later field controlled by an earlier field. On an initial pair $(h,d)$ this sequence yields $(h+d,d)$. It uses just one interchange. There are $a$ ones, which proves the claim. In particular, the number of recursive calls is the rational rank $a$; temporary tapes used for the other operations do not multiply that count.

adds.name: field groups
adds.meaning: the two ordered groups of $m$ address fields forming the two chunks, every $H_i$ before every $D_j$

adds.name: field radix
adds.meaning: the fixed odd prime in which the address fields are written, avoiding all denominators of the fixed rational matrices

adds.name: field width
adds.meaning: the number of radix-$q$ digits in one field, so each field ranges over $[q^b]$

adds.name: edge rank
adds.meaning: the rational rank of the edge matrix, equal to the number of smaller interchanges it needs

adds.name: partial permutation
adds.meaning: the $0/1$ matrix with exactly $a$ ones, at most one per row and column, in the factorization $A=E_1\Pi E_2$

children.claim: Given fixed circuit data with $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$ for every input role and $s<Wm$, and a rational $\tau\in(0,1)$ with $s/W<m^\tau$, two disjoint contiguous chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits, preceded by a row field of length divisible by $W^k$, can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time on a fixed number of tapes, with a constant independent of all field lengths.
children.method: Split whole rows cyclically into $W$ role streams of volume $V/W$; on each circuit edge apply the shear $\Phi_{A_e}$ by the factorization lemma, recursively interchanging each pivot pair of $b=e/m$ digit fields; execute gates pointwise; merge the roles back to obtain $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every row; complete the interchange with two linear updates; bound the per-node overhead by $O(V)$ with a depth-first schedule and solve the recurrence $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$.

motivation.text: The frame identity makes every role receive the same shear once the endpoint matrices differ by $I_m$, the rank of each edge difference counts the smaller interchanges, and distributing rows among the $W$ roles gives each recursive call volume $V/W$, which is what converts $s<Wm$ into a saving per unit of volume.

children.claim: Splitting whole rows cyclically into $W$ role streams within each prefix, with row $r=Wg+(w-1)$ sent to stream $w$ as row $g$, yields streams of exactly the same remaining shape, including the full ranges of $H$ and $D$, each of logical volume $V/W$ and with row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

quote.quote: Split whole rows cyclically into $W$ role streams within each prefix preceding the row field. Write the original row number as $r=Wg+(w-1)$ with $1\le w\le W$; stream $w$ has row number $g$. These streams have exactly the same remaining shape, including the full ranges of $H$ and $D$. Each has logical volume $V/W$, and its row count is divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

children.claim: With the frame $\Phi_M$ at a vertex with matrix $M$, a common address permutation commutes with every pointwise bit gate, the logical arrays are $g_w=\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w$ with no initial tape operation, and the physical output is $f'_{\rho(w)}=\Phi_{M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}}\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w=\Phi_{I_m}f_w$; merging row $g$ of role $\rho(w)$ back to row $Wg+(w-1)$ undoes $\rho$, so the result is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned to scratch roles whose initial values were arbitrary.

quote.quote: The row split supplies the common address set used in the frame identity~\eqref{eq:common-frame-identity}. Here the frame at a vertex with matrix $M$ is the address permutation $\Phi_M$, and every edge changes it by $\Phi_{M'-M}$. The same invariant proof applies because a common address permutation commutes with every pointwise bit gate. For the physical input arrays $f_w$, the logical arrays are $g_w=\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w$; this only specifies their interpretation, with no initial tape operation. The logical circuit routes $g_w$ to role $\rho(w)$. Thus its physical output satisfies \[ f'_{\rho(w)} =\Phi_{M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}} \Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w =\Phi_{I_m}f_w, \] by~\eqref{eq:finite-shear-contract}. Merge by returning row $g$ of output role $\rho(w)$ to the original row $Wg+(w-1)$ within the same preceding prefix. This undoes $\rho$ and restores row order. The result is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: The full interchange is $D\leftarrow D-H$, $H\leftarrow H+D$, $D\leftarrow H-D$ componentwise, which sends $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$; only the middle shear uses the circuit, and the other two updates target the later group at linear cost.

quote.quote: To interchange the two full chunks, perform \[ D\leftarrow D-H,\qquad H\leftarrow H+D,\qquad D\leftarrow H-D, \] componentwise. Only the middle shear uses the circuit. The other two updates target the later group and have linear cost. The transformation sends $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$.

children.claim: The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly $s$, each on one role stream of volume $V/W$ with all other fields as spectators; splitting, merging, gates and triangular operations cost $O(V)$ because their number is fixed, so if $F_k$ bounds time divided by logical volume then $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$.

quote.quote: The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly $s$. Each acts on one role stream of volume $V/W$, retaining all other fields as spectators. Splitting, merging, gates, and triangular operations have total cost $O(V)$ because their number is fixed. Below we verify that scheduling the recursive calls on fixed tapes also costs $O(V)$ at this node. Thus if $F_k$ is a uniform upper bound for time divided by logical volume, then \begin{equation} \label{eq:swap-recurrence} F_0=O(1),\qquad F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1).

children.claim: For $a=s/W<m^\tau$ the geometric sum $\sum_{j=0}^ka^j$ is $O(m^{k\tau})$: if $a\le1$ it is at most $k+1=O(m^{k\tau})$, and if $a>1$ it is $O(a^k)$; hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

quote.quote: For $a=s/W<m^\tau$ the geometric sum $\sum_{j=0}^k a^j$ is $O(m^{k\tau})$. If $a\le1$, the sum is at most $k+1=O(m^{k\tau})$; if $a>1$, it is $O(a^k)$. Hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Each push, pop, copy, positioning operation, or erasure moves $O(V)$ symbols at a parent node. There are only the fixed number $s$ of child calls. This gives precisely the additional $O(V)$ term claimed above, even though each child itself has volume $V/W$. Temporary storage is therefore not substituted for logical volume in the factor $s/W$.

children.claim: There are a fixed $0<\tau<1$ and one fixed multitape procedure that, for all positive integers $P,G,B$ and $u\ge1$, applies the address permutation $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$ to an arbitrary bit array on $[P]\times[2^u]\times[G]\times[2^u]\times[B]$ in $O(Vu^\tau)$ steps, $V=PGB\,2^{2u}$, including shape processing, all padding and unpadding, and workspace cleanup.
children.method: Supply the row field from the top $\rho=O(\log(2e))$ digits of the two chunks, pad rows to a multiple of $W^k$, write the remaining width in base $m$ and apply the power-width interchange to each corresponding pair of pieces, then unpad and separate the high parts again; handle binary chunks by numerical padding of each range to $[q^e]$, and widths differing by one bit by one single-bit move.

motivation.text: The power-width proposition needs a row field divisible by $W^k$ and widths that are powers of $m$; a few high digits of the chunks themselves supply the rows at logarithmic cost, and a base-$m$ expansion of the width gives a geometric sum of power-width costs dominated by its top term.

quote.quote: We have proved the fast operation for power widths with enough rows. Rows for a general array can be supplied by a few of its own high digits. Their movement will cost less than the final bound.

children.claim: With $k=\lceil\log_me\rceil$ and $\rho=\lceil k\log W/(2\log q)\rceil$, exchanging and joining the top $\rho$ digits of each chunk forms a row field of range $R=q^{2\rho}\ge W^k$ before both remaining chunks at cost $O(V\rho)$, and appending zero rows within each prefix to $R'=W^k\lceil R/W^k\rceil<2R$ keeps the padded logical volume below $2V$.

quote.quote: In the two middle orders, the first two fields form a row field of range \[ R=q^{2\rho}\ge W^k \] before both remaining chunks. The joining moves preserve the order of the remaining digits and the gap field. Exchanging and joining the high parts costs $O(V\rho)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:elementary-streams}. Append zero rows, separately within each preceding prefix, until the row count is \[ R'=W^k\left\lceil R/W^k\right\rceil<2R. \] This changes the row field's length; it need not remain a power of $q$ during the computation. The padded logical volume is less than $2V$.

children.claim: Writing $e-\rho=\sum_{j=0}^ka_jm^j$ in base $m$ and applying the power-width interchange to the $a_j$ corresponding pairs of width $m^j$, all with the common row field of length $R'$, the costs sum to $O(V)\sum_ja_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau)$ because $a_j<m$ and $m^k<me$; every completed call preserves its row address, so padded zero rows remain zero and no genuine row mixes with a padded one.

quote.quote: Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:power-interchange} to each corresponding pair. All these calls use the same row field of length $R'$, which is divisible by each required $W^j$. At completion every call preserves its row address, so it neither mixes genuine rows with padded rows nor depends on the values used for padding. The padded zero rows remain zero at these completed-call boundaries. The sum of the costs is bounded by \[ O(V)\sum_j a_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau). \] The fixed bound $a_j<m$ and the inequality $m^k<me$ make this a geometric sum of the stated order.

children.claim: For binary chunks, pad each chunk range numerically from $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$ with $e$ least such that $q^e\ge2^u$, a fixed volume factor below $q^2$ that preserves the order of existing entries; interchange, then scan away the entries with an invalid coordinate; since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Finally, for binary chunks let $e$ be the least integer with $q^e\ge2^u$. Pad each of the two chunk ranges numerically from $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$, putting zero in an entry if either chunk coordinate is invalid. The increase in volume is less than $q^2$, a fixed factor. The padding is a nested scan through consecutive valid and invalid intervals, with their lengths prepared from the shape. It costs $O(V)$ with a constant depending on $q$. Lexicographic radix-$q$ order of $[q^e]$ is its numerical order, just as binary order of $[2^u]$ is its numerical order. Padding therefore preserves the order of the existing entries without converting the digits of every address. The completed interchange preserves the set on which both chunk coordinates lie below $2^u$. Scan away the other entries to recover the desired binary array. Since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

children.claim: Chunks whose widths differ by one bit are interchanged by one single-bit move of the longer chunk's leading bit, costing $O(V)$, plus one equal-width interchange, with the gap field $g$ remaining between the two full chunks; no unrestricted array transpose is used.

quote.quote: Here the first step moves $d_0$ immediately before $H$, and the second interchanges $H,D$. In each case $g$ remains between the two full chunks in the final order. If $H,D$ are empty, the indicated equal-width interchange is the identity. Each case uses one single-bit move, costing $O(V)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:elementary-streams}, in addition to the equal-width interchange. No unrestricted array transpose is being used in these operations.

children.salient: Although the final effect is an exact permutation of the array, the intermediate steps form XOR combinations of the data bits, which places the procedure outside models restricted to moving data without computation, where an $n\log n$ lower bound is known.

children.claim: For $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$, $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$, $r=2^{\Theta(p/d)}$ and $1\le D\le d$, one fixed procedure applies the tensor product $\mathcal H$ of $H_0=\frac12\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ on the selected bit $\rho$ of each of $D$ consecutive $K$-bit address chunks, coefficientwise on polynomial records of $r$ disk-grid coefficients, returning $Q_p(\mathcal Hz)$ in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time with $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}<1$, with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ and the unit disk preserved.
children.method: Write $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ with the kernel $C=aI+bX$; evaluate $C^{\otimes e}$ by the complex network, whose phase frames make each edge a product of translation kernels implemented as binary basis changes by packed selected-bit additions plus $s_{\rm c}$ recursive calls on slots of $e/m$ chunks and $1/W_{\rm c}$ of the volume; take rows from the first $q_0$ chunks; unroll the recurrence; bound the growth of the exact dyadic values so that one guarded width $O(p)$ suffices; truncate once at the end.

motivation.text: A round of the multidimensional transform applies a butterfly on every participating axis; done one axis at a time that is $D$ passes over the whole array, so the layer must be applied simultaneously, by the same network recursion that saved a power for address interchange.

quote.quote: We will obtain cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with $\lambda'<1$ and $V$ the logical bit volume, whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

children.claim: With $C=H\mathsf SH=aI+bX$, $a=(1+i)/2$, $b=(1-i)/2$, the Gaussian-dyadic identities $H_0=b\mathsf SC\mathsf S$ and $C^{-1}=-iZCZ$ hold; an edge from label $U_-$ to $U_+$ has frame change $\prod_j(aI+bX_{v_j})^{\epsilon_j}$ over an orthonormal basis of its residual, which after a binary change of coordinates $\mathcal P_M$ becomes $\prod_jC_{e_j}^{\epsilon_j}$ on coordinate directions; so one network invocation on $e=mf$ selected axes yields $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role with exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls on $f$ axes each, and $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ converts the completed $C$-layer to normalized butterflies.
children.method: Conjugate the translation kernels by the address permutation $\mathcal P_M$ whose first columns are the residual basis; implement $M$ by elementary row additions on the selected bits of whole slots; obtain each inverse child from one forward child by $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}$; wrap the endpoint $C^{\otimes D}$ in the diagonal phases $\mathcal S_D$ and the scalar $b^D$.

motivation.text: Working with the kernel $C$ instead of $H_0$ keeps every intermediate value an exact Gaussian dyadic, and the Hadamard conjugations defining the phase frames are only proof devices, so the machine executes nothing but signed shifts, halvings, multiplications by $i$ and address moves.

quote.quote: These identities use only Gaussian dyadic coefficients. The Hadamard matrices in the definition of $\mathcal C_U$ are used to prove identities; they need not be executed by the machine.

children.claim: Extending the residual basis $v_1,\ldots,v_{\rho_{\rm edge}}$ to a basis of $\mathbb F_2^m$ as the first columns of $M$, the conjugation $\mathcal P_MX_v\mathcal P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}$ turns the edge identity into $\mathcal C_{U_+}\mathcal C_{U_-}^{-1}=\mathcal P_M(\prod_jC_{e_j}^{\epsilon_j})\mathcal P_M^{-1}$ on standard directions; $M$ need only be invertible, not orthogonal.

quote.quote: Extend $v_1,\ldots,v_{\rho_{\rm edge}}$ to a basis of $\mathbb F_2^m$ and take these vectors as the first $\rho_{\rm edge}$ columns of $M$. The displayed edge identity then becomes \begin{equation}\label{eq:phase-edge-coordinate} \mathcal C_{U_+}\mathcal C_{U_-}^{-1} =\mathcal P_M\left(\prod_{j=1}^{\rho_{\rm edge}}C_{e_j}^{\epsilon_j}\right) \mathcal P_M^{-1}, \end{equation} where $e_j$ is the $j$th standard basis vector. The matrix $M$ need not preserve the dot product: equation~\eqref{eq:phase-conjugation} only uses its invertibility.

children.claim: On a group of $e=mf$ consecutive chunks divided into $m$ slots of $f$ chunks, apply $\mathcal P_M^{-1}$ to each column, then $(C^{\epsilon_h})^{\otimes f}$ to the $f$ selected bits of slot $h$ as one child operation for each $h\le\rho_{\rm edge}$, then $\mathcal P_M$; a negative kernel needs only one forward child because $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}$, and all inverse wrappers are address signs and constant fourth-root phases adding no recursive calls.

quote.quote: To implement \eqref{eq:phase-edge-coordinate} on the group, first apply $\mathcal P_M^{-1}$ separately to each column. For each $1\le h\le\rho_{\rm edge}$, apply $(C^{\epsilon_h})^{\otimes f}$ to the $f$ bits $x_{h,0},\ldots,x_{h,f-1}$. This is one child operation on the $f$ axes in slot $h$. Finally apply $\mathcal P_M$ to every column. A negative directional kernel still requires only one forward child, because \begin{equation}\label{eq:phase-inverse-child} (C^{-1})^{\otimes f} =(-i)^f Z^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}. \end{equation} The rightmost phase is applied first. All inverse wrappers are address signs and constant fourth-root phases, so they add no recursive calls.

children.claim: Any $M\in\operatorname{GL}(m,\mathbb F_2)$ is a product of at most $m(m-1)+3m$ elementary row additions, a fixed number since $m$ is fixed; adding row $h'$ to row $h$ in every column applies $x_{h,j}\leftarrow x_{h,j}\oplus x_{h',j}$ for all $0\le j<f$, changing corresponding selected positions in two whole slots, which the packed address operation performs together.

quote.quote: Gaussian elimination expresses any $M\in\operatorname{GL}(m,\mathbb F_2)$ as a product of at most $m(m-1)+3m$ elementary row additions: one clears at most $m-1$ other entries per pivot, and each row swap is three row additions. Reversing the elimination gives the required product since each row addition is an involution. The number is a constant because $m$ is fixed. Adding row $h'$ to row $h$ in every column applies $x_{h,j}\leftarrow x_{h,j}\mathbin\oplus x_{h',j}$ for every $0\le j<f$. Thus one row addition changes corresponding selected positions in two whole slots. The packed address operation proved below performs all of these XORs together.

children.claim: Summing the residual dimensions gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls on $f=e/m$ axes each; the source and sink $Z_{a,f}$ signs with the scalar $i^{27f}$ turn every endpoint kernel into a forward one, and negating the prescribed bank and undoing its exchange returns $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role, including roles whose initial scratch values were arbitrary.

quote.quote: Apply the finite network with these column frames to a group of $e=mf$ selected axes. Summing its residual dimensions gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot. The source and sink $Z_{a,f}$ signs, together with the scalar $i^{27f}$ at each affected sink, turn every endpoint kernel into a forward one. Negating the prescribed physical bank and undoing its exchange returns each result to its original role. Proposition~\ref{prop:complex-motif-interface} therefore gives $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role, including roles whose initial scratch values were arbitrary.

children.claim: With $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\cdots+x_D}z(x)$ on the selected bits, $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, where $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a binary shift and fourth-root phase with at most one factor $b$, so the complete parallel butterfly layer is exact up to its prescribed final truncation.

quote.quote: Applying \eqref{eq:phase-basic-identities} on all selected coordinates gives \begin{equation}\label{eq:phase-butterfly-layer} H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_D C^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D. \end{equation} The scalar is \[ b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}, \] so it is a binary shift and fourth-root phase, with at most one further factor $b$. All phases, inverse wrappers, and scalar corrections above are exact Gaussian dyadic operations. Thus, once the physical binary basis changes and recursive stream layout are supplied, the complete parallel butterfly layer is exact up to its prescribed final truncation.

children.salient: A decreasing edge, whose kernel is an inverse $C^{-1}$, still costs exactly one forward child call, because $C^{-1}=-iZCZ$ turns it into a forward kernel wrapped in address signs and a constant phase.

children.claim: On $R$-bit records on $[N_0]\times[2^L]_{\chi_1}\times[N_1]\times[2^L]_{\chi_2}\times[N_2]\times[2^L]_{\chi_3}\times[N_3]$ with $L=fK$, $K\ge6$, one fixed procedure performs $y_{j_i}\leftarrow y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$ at the $f$ selected positions $j_i=\rho+iK$ at once, preserves spectators, other chunk bits and every payload, restores the chunk $z$ for every initial value, and costs $O(V(L^\tau+1)+MA_{\rm rect}^3+\delta_{\rm bad}MA_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect}))$, which is $O(V(L^\tau+1))$ when $R$ exceeds every fixed polynomial in $p$, $f\le d\le p$ and $K/\log p\to\infty$.
children.method: Apply eight whole-chunk cyclic shifts whose offsets are sums of $2^{j_i}$ over selected bits of the other two chunks; their composition $S_0$ equals the ideal XOR permutation $T_0$ except on a guard-violating set $\mathcal B$ of fraction at most $80(f-1)2^{-K}$; since $T_0S_0^{-1}$ permutes $\mathcal B$, extract those records with destination ranks, radix sort them and reinsert; finish the top position by an elementary two-bit XOR.

motivation.text: A cyclic shift of a whole chunk range by a control-dependent offset is a linear-cost primitive, and adding $2^{j_i}$ to a chunk flips bit $j_i$ unless a carry crosses a segment boundary, so a packed addition is right except where guard digits are near their boundary; that exceptional set is small and determined by addresses alone, so it is repaired deterministically.

quote.quote: The construction first uses a constant number of cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges, then corrects an explicitly bounded set of addresses. The correction depends only on addresses, so the time bound is worst-case over all payloads.

children.claim: For a Boolean control $c$ and arbitrary integers $u,w$, the eight parity-controlled additions compose the cycles $(00\ 01\ 10)$ and $(01\ 10\ 11)$ on each parity square into $(00\ 10)(01\ 11)$, so the output is $(u',w')=(u+c(1-2(u\bmod2)),w)$: the parity of $u$ flips exactly when $c=1$, both quotients by two are preserved, the auxiliary integer $w$ is restored, and each coordinate moves by at most four.

quote.quote: Consequently the complete output is \begin{equation} \label{eq:eight-packed-result} (u',w')= \bigl(u+c(1-2(u\bmod2)),\ w\bigr). \end{equation} Here $u\bmod2\in\{0,1\}$, also for negative $u$. Thus the parity of $u$ is flipped precisely when $c=1$, both quotients under division by two are preserved, and the arbitrary auxiliary integer $w$ is restored. Each coordinate is updated four times by at most one, so its displacement from its initial value is at most four, even if an intermediate point leaves its starting quotient square. The weaker bound eight will suffice below.

children.claim: Outside the set $\mathcal B$ of addresses where some used guard value violates $10\le g\le2^{K-1}-11$, each $K$-bit segment starts in $[20,2^K-21]$ and a displacement of eight keeps it inside $[0,2^K-1]$, so no segment carries into or borrows from the next and the composed shifts $S_0$ agree with the ideal permutation $T_0$; the union bound over the $2(f-1)$ guards, each with twenty excluded values out of $2^{K-1}$, gives $|\mathcal B|\le\delta_{\rm bad}M$ with $\delta_{\rm bad}=\min\{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}\}$, independently of record values.

quote.quote: At an address outside $\mathcal B$, each segment initially lies in $[20,2^K-21]$. Even displacement eight keeps it inside $[0,2^K-1]$. Inductively, each packed addition therefore agrees with all the independent segment additions: no segment carries into or borrows from the next segment. When $f>1$, the bits below $j_0$ and above the highest used segment are untouched as well. By \eqref{eq:eight-packed-result}, $S_0$ then agrees with the ideal permutation $T_0$ that performs the required XORs at $j_0,\ldots,j_{f-2}$ and fixes all other address coordinates. There are exactly twenty excluded values for each guard in \eqref{eq:packed-guard-interval}. Since its complete range has $2^{K-1}$ values, the union bound over the $2(f-1)$ guards gives \begin{equation} \label{eq:packed-bad-fraction} |\mathcal B|\le\delta_{\rm bad}M. \end{equation} Indeed, the complete $y,z$ ranges give the same guard distribution at each choice of spectator coordinates. No record value enters this count.

children.claim: $T_0$ preserves all guard values and hence $\mathcal B$; both $T_0$ and $S_0$ are bijections agreeing off $\mathcal B$, so $S_0(\mathcal B^c)=\mathcal B^c$ and $S_0(\mathcal B)=\mathcal B$, and $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B$.

quote.quote: The ideal map $T_0$ preserves all guard values and therefore preserves $\mathcal B$. Both $T_0$ and $S_0$ are bijections, and they agree off $\mathcal B$. Taking complements in the finite rectangle gives \[ S_0(\mathcal B^c)=T_0(\mathcal B^c)=\mathcal B^c, \qquad S_0(\mathcal B)=\mathcal B. \] Thus $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B$.

children.claim: Each rotation is realized by moving its target chunk last with at most two width-$L$ chunk swaps at $O(VL^\tau)$ and one $O(V)$ controlled shift whose offset is computed from the two control values in $L^{O(1)}$ time; the exceptional records are extracted with $O(A_{\rm rect})$-bit destination ranks, stably radix sorted and reinserted in one scan; so the movement costs $O(V(L^\tau+1))$, the record scans $O(MA_{\rm rect}^3+V)$ and the sort $O(|\mathcal B|A_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect}))$, and after division by $V=MR$ the extra terms are $A_{\rm rect}^3/R\to0$ and $O(p^22^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$ under the family bounds.

quote.quote: The movement costs $O(V(L^\tau+1))$. A fixed number of full record scans costs $O(MA_{\rm rect}^3+V)$, and the at most $A_{\rm rect}$ radix passes cost $O(|\mathcal B|A_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect}))$; skip them when the extracted bank is empty. The initial descriptor has a fixed number of canonical integers of $O(A_{\rm rect})$ bits, so its preparation is covered by $O(MA_{\rm rect}^3)$. All counters, positioning, rewinds, and cleanup are included. Equation~\eqref{eq:packed-bad-fraction} proves \eqref{eq:packed-rectangle-time} on a fixed number of tapes. After division by $V=MR$, its additional terms are bounded by $A_{\rm rect}^3/R$ and $80(f-1)2^{-K}A_{\rm rect}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R)$. Under the stated family bounds the first tends to zero, and the second is $O(p^2 2^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$. This proves the final assertion.

children.salient: Eight controlled rotations flip the selected bit of each of $f-1$ segments simultaneously while an arbitrary auxiliary chunk returns exactly to its initial value, and the repair of the exceptional addresses never reads a payload, so the bound is worst-case over all data.

children.claim: Running the network on $W$ role streams whose rows come from the first $q_0$ chunks, the normalized cost $F(e)$ of a $C$-layer on $e$ chunks satisfies $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$ with $F(e)=O(e)$ for $e<d^\beta$, $\beta=1/2$, and summing over the base-$m$ pieces of $D-q_0$ gives total normalized cost $O(d^{\lambda'})$ for any fixed $\max\{\lambda,\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)\}<\lambda'<1$.
children.method: Apply $C$ individually on the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks and use their bits as a row index of range at least $W^{k_0}$; charge the basis changes at a node by the packed lemma; unroll the recurrence with $a=s/W\le m^\sigma<m^\lambda$ and stop at $e<d^\beta$.

motivation.text: The power-width recurrence needs rows divisible by $W^k$; a layer has no row field, but the first $q_0$ chunks, processed individually at $O(V\log d)$ cost, provide one, and the per-node overhead $(eK)^\tau$ is a smaller power than $\lambda$ by the choice $\tau(1+c/\beta)<\lambda$, so the geometric sum is dominated by the top node.

children.claim: Applying $C$ individually on the selected bits of the first $q_0$ chunks in $O(V\log d)$ time leaves a complete consecutive block whose concatenated bits form a row index of range $R_{\rm row}=2^{q_0K}\ge W^{k_0}$; padding rows to the next multiple of $W^{k_0}$ grows the volume by at most two, and at depth $j\le k_0$ the row count is divisible by $W^{k_0-j}$.

quote.quote: Otherwise apply \(C\) individually on the selected bits of the first \(q_0\) chunks, in \(O(V\log d)\) time. These chunks remain a complete consecutive address block before all the remaining chunks; regard their concatenated bits as one row index. Its range has length \(R_{\rm row}=2^{q_0K}\ge W^{k_0}\), since \(K\ge1\) for sufficiently large \(p\) and \(q_0K\ge k_0\log_2W\). Within each preceding prefix, add the same number of zero rows to reach the next multiple of \(W^{k_0}\); the volume grows by a factor at most two. At any recursive depth \(j\le k_0\), the row count is divisible by \(W^{k_0-j}\).

children.claim: With $F(e)$ the time divided by the current logical volume, $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$ and $F(e)=O(e)$ for $e<d^\beta$: the $s$ children run on volume $V/W$ each, giving the factor $s/W$, and at an internal node $K\le d^c\le e^{c/\beta}$ makes the overhead $O(e^{\tau(1+c/\beta)}+1)=O(e^\lambda)$.

quote.quote: Stop recursion when \(e<d^\beta\) and apply the \(e\) \(C\) kernels individually. If \(F(e)\) denotes time divided by the current logical stream volume, then \[ F(e)\le (s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1), \qquad F(e)=O(e)\quad(e<d^\beta). \] Indeed, the \(s\) child calls are executed on streams of volume \(V/W\), so their total cost is \(s(V/W)F(e/m)\). Dividing by the current volume \(V\) gives the factor \(s/W\). At an internal node \(e\ge d^\beta\), hence \(K\le d^c\le e^{c/\beta}\). The overhead is therefore \(O(e^{\tau(1+c/\beta)}+1)=O(e^\lambda)\).

children.claim: Since $a=s/W\le m^\sigma<m^\lambda$, the internal costs sum to $Ce^\lambda\sum_j(a/m^\lambda)^j=O(e^\lambda)$ and the leaves contribute $O(a^ju)\le O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)})$; over at most $(m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_md\rfloor)$ pieces plus the row preprocessing the total is $O(\log(2d)[d^\lambda+d^{\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)}+1])=O(d^{\lambda'})$.

quote.quote: Write \(D-q_0=\sum_j a_jm^j\) in base \(m\), with \(0\le a_j<m\). Partition the remaining chunks into \(a_j\) consecutive pieces containing \(m^j\) chunks for each \(j\). There are at most \((m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_m d\rfloor)\) pieces. Adding their costs and the row preprocessing gives \[ O\!\left(\log(2d) \bigl[d^\lambda+d^{\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)}+1\bigr]\right) =O(d^{\lambda'}) \] for any fixed \[ \max\{\lambda,\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)\}<\lambda'<1.

children.claim: A value at arithmetic depth $\ell$ lies in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell$, and the depth within a layer is below $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil$ with $C_1=20$; choosing $\epsilon C_1<1$ with $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$ gives $\Delta=o(p)$, so the full guarded coefficient width is $O(p)$ and every intermediate coefficient is represented exactly.

quote.quote: Choose \(\epsilon C_1<1\). Since \(d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)\), \(\Delta=o(p)\), and the full coefficient width is \(O(p)\), as required in the time analysis. Addition, signed shifts, copying and phase changes consequently take \(O(p)\) bit operations per coefficient.

children.claim: The procedure returns $Q_p(\mathcal Hz)$ in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time; every row of $\mathcal H$ has absolute row sum one, so disk arrays map to disk arrays, and componentwise truncation toward zero preserves the disk with error less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote: Finally, every row of $\mathcal H$ has absolute row sum one. Thus $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, and componentwise truncation preserves that disk and has error less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$: truncation cannot increase the absolute value of either component, and changes each by less than $2^{-p}$. The truncated numerators have magnitude at most $2^p$, so the supplied component width can hold them.

children.salient: The whole layer is evaluated exactly in Gaussian dyadics through intermediate operators that are not contractions, with only one truncation at the end, so a simultaneous layer on up to $d$ axes has the same error $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ as a single butterfly.

children.claim: For arrays $f,g$ of disk-grid records in $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ on $\prod_{i<d}\mathbb Z/t_i\mathbb Z$ with $M=\prod_{i<d}t_i$ and $T=rM$, the normalized convolution $\mathcal M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/T$ has an approximation, returned in the original order, with error less than $\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$, $\ell=\log_2r$, at cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}+\log(rp)])$, and the output is a disk array when one operand has norm at most $\rho<1$ with that error bound at most $1-\rho$.
children.method: Define synthetic transforms over the ring whose roots of unity $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$ act by signed coefficient shifts; perform two forward transforms that write outputs in the retained order $LB$; multiply corresponding records pointwise by signed packing divided by $r$; apply the opposite procedure, which consumes that order; scale exactly by $M$; add the three transform errors and one truncation through contractions.

motivation.text: Roots of unity in the ring are signed coefficient shifts, so transform arithmetic needs no complex multiplications; and because a record permutation commutes with pointwise products, the bit-reversed layout order never has to be undone between the forward transforms and the opposite one.

quote.quote: Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation $LB$ to both operands. We may therefore multiply the forward outputs in their retained order and pass that order directly to the opposite procedure.

children.claim: With $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$ for a power of two $t\mid2r$, the transforms $(F_t^\pm z)_j=\frac1t\sum_k\omega_t^{\pm jk}z_k$ are contractions since every power of $\omega_t$ is an isometry, and $\sum_{k=0}^{t-1}\omega_t^{jk}$ equals $t$ when $t\mid j$ and $0$ otherwise, because for $j=2^vj_0$ with $j_0$ odd the substitution $k\mapsto k+t/2^{v+1}$ multiplies the sum by $y^{rj_0}=-1$ and the ring has no two-torsion; hence $F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I$.

quote.quote: Only the second case needs proof. Write $j=2^v j_0$ with $j_0$ odd and $0\leq v<\log_2t$. Replacing $k$ by $k+t/2^{v+1}$ modulo $t$ permutes the summands and multiplies their sum by $y^{rj_0}=-1$. Hence the sum is zero, since the additive group of $\mathcal R_r$ has no two-torsion. Expanding the composite transforms and applying this identity proves the final formula.

children.salient: Every twiddle multiplication is a signed cyclic shift of a coefficient list, exact and free of real arithmetic, even though the ring has zero divisors and the usual division by $\omega_t^j-1$ is unavailable.

children.claim: The decimation-in-frequency recursion writes $(F_t^-z)_j$ into slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$ without moving whole frequency indices, and the procedure traversing the recursion in reverse composes with it to $I/t$ because $H_0^2=I/2$ at each of the $a=\log_2t$ levels; so the two exact procedures implement $B_tF_t^-$ and $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$, and on several axes a round groups as a parallel butterfly $\mathcal H$ followed by one recordwise monomial $J_E$, a contraction followed by an isometry.

quote.quote: The procedure consuming this stored order traverses the recursion in reverse: first process the two smaller branches, then apply the inverse monomial to the second branch, and finally apply $H_0$. Each forward level is invertible, since both its butterfly and its monomial are invertible. As $H_0^2=I/2$, the reversed level is half the inverse of the corresponding forward level. There are $a=\log_2t$ levels, so the reverse procedure composed with $B_tF_t^-$ is $2^{-a}I=I/t$. Lemma~\ref{lem:synthetic-characters} gives the same composite for $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$ with $B_tF_t^-$. The forward procedure is invertible, so these two reverse operators agree. Thus the two exact procedures implement \begin{equation} B_tF_t^-,\qquad F_t^+B_t^{-1}, \label{eq:stored-opposite} \end{equation} respectively.

children.salient: The forward transform leaves its outputs in bit-reversed order and the opposite transform consumes exactly that order, so no frequency permutation is ever executed.

children.claim: For $t_i\in\{2^{\ell-1},2^\ell\}$, $d\ell\le C_\ell p$ and $1\le K\le\ell-1$, a positional layout permutation $L$ of record addresses lets every transform round be one simultaneous butterfly layer, so that the forward procedure realizes exactly $LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$ and the opposite one $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$, each with error less than $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$, disk-grid output, and cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$.
children.method: Move $O(dK)$ named slots to a prefix by single-bit moves; reorder the remaining $K$-bit chunks from axis-major to chunk-major by at most $Dq-1$ chunk exchanges; run the rounds as simultaneous layers with the combined twiddle monomial $J_E$ applied exactly after each; process the prefix-slot rounds individually; truncate once per round and identify the stored order.

motivation.text: The simultaneous layer needs the selected bit of each participating axis at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks, so the axis-major address order must be interleaved chunk by chunk; the chunk interchange does this at cost $O(TpK^\tau)$ per exchange, sublinear in $K$.

quote.quote: To apply Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} in a transform round, we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

children.claim: Listing the slots $(i,\ell-1)$ of the long axes and then the $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$ lowest slots of every axis, and moving each immediately after the prefix formed so far, uses $O(dK)$ single-bit moves costing $O(TpdK)$ and leaves each axis as $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$ consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

quote.quote: Form a list of the slots to move to a prefix. First list $(i,\ell-1)$ for the length-$2^\ell$ axes in increasing $i$. Then list $(i,h)$ for $h=b-1,\ldots,0$, and within each $h$ in increasing $i$; this second list is empty if $b=0$. Move each listed slot immediately after the prefix already formed, leaving all other slots in their relative order. There are at most $D(b+1)=O(dK)$ listed slots, so the moves cost $O(TpdK)$. A descriptor records the physical position of every named slot. The part of each axis left outside the prefix now consists of $q$ consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

children.claim: Reordering the chunks from $(1,1),\ldots,(1,q),(2,1),\ldots,(D,q)$ to $(1,1),(2,1),\ldots,(D,1),(1,2),\ldots,(D,q)$ by scanning target positions and exchanging the chunk present with the required one uses at most $Dq-1$ width-$K$ chunk exchanges at $O(TpK^\tau)$ each, total $O(Tp\,pK^{\tau-1})$; these moves define $L$, and recording them in reverse gives $L^{-1}$.

quote.quote: To obtain this order, scan its target positions from left to right. At each position except the last, exchange the chunk currently there with the required chunk if they differ. This uses at most $Dq-1$ exchanges of width-$K$ address chunks, even when the chunks are nonadjacent. Each costs $O(TpK^\tau)$, so all these exchanges cost \[ O\bigl(Tp\,DqK^\tau\bigr) =O\bigl(Tp\,pK^{\tau-1}\bigr). \] These prefix moves and chunk exchanges define $L$. We use the same letter for its induced record permutation: a record at address $x$ moves to address $Lx$, while its polynomial suffix stays intact. Recording the inverse operations in reverse order gives $L^{-1}$ with the same cost.

children.claim: In a round at named position $h$ in the remaining chunks the selected bit has offset $(h-b)\bmod K$ in each of the $D$ chunks with the same index $j$, every combination of the other bits occurs, so the layer sees the complete set $[P]\times[2^K]^D\times[S]$ with $\log_2(2M)\le C_Mp$; the simultaneous-layer procedure therefore applies at $O(Tpd^{\lambda'})$ per round and $O(Tp\ell d^{\lambda'})$ in total.

quote.quote: For a position $h$ in the remaining chunks, the selected bit has offset $(h-b)\bmod K$, counted from the least significant bit, in each of the $D$ consecutive chunks with the same chunk index $j$. Let $n_P$ and $n_S$ be the numbers of record-address bits before and after that group. Every combination of those bits occurs, so the layer sees the complete address set \[ [P]\times[2^K]^D\times[S],\qquad P=2^{n_P},\quad S=2^{n_S},\quad n_P+DK+n_S=\sum_i a_i\leq D\ell=O(p). \] Thus its record count is $PS2^{DK}=M$ and $\log_2(2M)\leq(C_\ell+1)p=C_Mp$.

children.claim: Since $J_E$ is a signed coefficient permutation and truncation toward zero is odd, $J_EQ_p(\mathcal Hz)=Q_p(J_E\mathcal Hz)$, so each forward round returns exactly one truncation after the exact contraction round, and the opposite round likewise; a contraction does not increase the error and each truncation adds less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$, so at most $\ell$ rounds give error below $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ with the disk preserved.

quote.quote: Truncation toward zero is odd and acts separately on every real and imaginary part. Since $J_E$ is a signed coefficient permutation, it follows that \[ J_EQ_p(\mathcal H z)=Q_p(J_E\mathcal H z). \] Thus the actual forward call sequence returns exactly the result of truncating once after the exact contraction round. In the opposite direction, $J_E^{-1}$ first preserves the disk grid, and the layer call returns $Q_p(\mathcal HJ_E^{-1}z)$ directly. The rounds on prefix slots have the same forms, with one truncation, by their exact evaluation above. A contraction does not increase the norm of the difference between the computed and exact arrays; the single truncation then adds less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ by \eqref{eq:transform-truncate}. Both the contraction and truncation preserve the disk. Starting with zero error, at most $\ell$ rounds therefore give the claimed error and disk bounds. The layout permutations are isometries and add no numerical error.

children.claim: Executing operations on named slots after $L$ conjugates the exact logical procedures $\mathcal D_-=BF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$ and $\mathcal D_+=F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}$ by $L$; the forward procedure moves records by $L$ first and the opposite restores by $L^{-1}$ last, so their full exact operators are $LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$ and $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$, the forward entry of frequency $j$ being stored at $L(Bj)$.

quote.quote: Executing each operation on named slots after $L$ conjugates it by $L$. The forward procedure first moves the records by $L$, whereas the opposite procedure restores them by $L^{-1}$ after its reverse arithmetic. Their full exact operators are \[ (L\mathcal D_-L^{-1})L=LB F_{\boldsymbol t}^-, \qquad L^{-1}(L\mathcal D_+L^{-1}) =F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}. \] In particular, the forward entry with frequency address $j$ is stored at $L(Bj)$. The reverse arithmetic consumes the frequency branch coordinates and outputs the normalized opposite transform indexed by the original axis coordinates, which are still in layout $L$. The factor $B^{-1}$ is realized by that arithmetic; the final charged movement $L^{-1}$ restores axis-major physical order.

children.claim: For disk-grid polynomials $f,g\in\mathcal R_r$ with $r=2^\ell<2^p$, the exact Gaussian integer numerators of $fg$ and then $Q_p(fg/r)$ can be computed in $O(rp\log(rp))$ time on fixed tapes, with output a disk grid polynomial of error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ from $fg/r$.
children.method: Evaluate the four integer coefficient polynomials $a,b,c,e$ at $B_0=2^{4p}$ with signed carries into fixed-width blocks, multiply the four magnitudes with the established $O(N\log N)$ multiplier, extract coefficients by centered residues modulo $B_0$ since $|h_j|<B_0/2$, form $ac-be$ and $ae+bc$, reduce modulo $y^r+1$, and truncate after shifting by $p+\ell$ bits.

motivation.text: A product of polynomials with bounded integer coefficients is read off from one product of the integers obtained by evaluating at a large power of two, so the established $O(N\log N)$ multiplier serves as an ordinary subroutine on $O(rp)$-bit inputs, far shorter than $n$, and the improved theorem is not invoked recursively.

quote.quote: To multiply the polynomial records, we use the fixed-tape integer multiplier of Harvey and van der Hoeven~\cite[Theorem~1.1]{HarveyHoeven2021}, with cost $O(N\log(2N))$ on $N$-bit inputs. This is an independent subroutine.

children.claim: With $A_u=u(B_0)$ and $B_0=2^{4p}$, each $|A_u|<B_0^r/2$ fits in $4pr$ bits, the product $A_aA_c$ equals $h(B_0)$ for the ordinary polynomial product $h=ac$, and every coefficient satisfies $|h_j|\le r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2$, so after the lower coefficients are removed the next one is identified by its centered residue modulo $B_0$.

quote.quote: The bound \[ |A_u|\leq2^p\frac{B_0^r-1}{B_0-1}<B_0^r/2 \] shows that each magnitude fits in $4pr$ bits. Multiply the four pairs of absolute values using the established multiplier and restore each product's sign. The resulting integers are $A_aA_c,A_bA_e,A_aA_e,A_bA_c$. For example, if $h=ac$ is the ordinary product in $\mathbb Z[y]$, then \[ A_aA_c=(ac)(B_0)=\sum_{j=0}^{2r-2}h_jB_0^j. \] The other three evaluation products have the same form. Every coefficient in any of these ordinary polynomial products satisfies \begin{equation} |h_j|\leq r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2. \label{eq:packing-separation} \end{equation} After the lower coefficients have been removed from an evaluation, this strict bound identifies the next coefficient by its centered residue modulo $B_0$.

children.claim: Reading the product in $J=2r$ blocks with carries $\rho_j\in\{0,1\}$ and centered residues, the residual identity $\sum_{k\ge j}h_kB_0^{k-j}=\sum_{k\ge j}q_kB_0^{k-j}+\rho_j+\varepsilon B_0^{J-j}$ gives $\widehat h_j=h_j$ at every block, a negative product's final carry $1$ being canceled by its sign extension $\varepsilon=-1$, so extraction costs $O(rp)$.

quote.quote: For $j<J$, reduction modulo $B_0$ gives $h_j\equiv q_j+\rho_j\pmod{B_0}$. By \eqref{eq:packing-separation}, including the padded value $h_{J-1}=0$, the unique centered representative is $h_j$ itself. Thus $\widehat h_j=h_j$. Subtracting this coefficient and dividing the residual identity by $B_0$ gives the next identity, with exactly the displayed update for $\rho_{j+1}$. At $j=J$ the identity is $0=\rho_J+\varepsilon$. Hence a negative product has final carry $1$, canceled by its sign extension $\varepsilon=-1$; a nonnegative product has final carry zero. The machine implements the induction by reading one block and updating this constant-size carry at each step, so extraction costs $O(rp)$.

children.claim: Reducing modulo $y^r+1$ by subtracting the coefficient at $j+r$ from the one at $j$ makes each $H_j$ a sum of exactly $r$ signed products of Gaussian integers of modulus at most $2^p$, so $|H_j|\le r2^{2p}$, and the same triangle inequality gives $\|fg/r\|_\infty\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_\infty$: the normalized product of disk polynomials lies in the disk.

quote.quote: For each first input index $j_1\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, exactly one second index $j_2$ in that range satisfies $j_1+j_2\equiv j\pmod r$. Its sign is positive when $j_1+j_2=j$ and negative when $j_1+j_2=j+r$. Thus each resulting Gaussian integer coefficient $H_j$ is a sum of exactly $r$ signed products of Gaussian integer input coefficients of modulus at most $2^p$. Consequently \[ |H_j|\leq r2^{2p}. \] The same triangle inequality before imposing the disk bound gives $\|fg/r\|_\infty\leq\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_\infty$; in particular the normalized product of disk polynomials lies in the disk.

children.claim: Expanding the finite sums, $F_{\boldsymbol t}^-(f*g)=M(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-f)(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-g)$ and $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+F_{\boldsymbol t}^-=I/M$ give $MF_{\boldsymbol t}^+((F_{\boldsymbol t}^-f)(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-g)/r)=(f*g)/(rM)$; since $LB$ permutes records leaving their polynomial suffixes intact, $P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v)$, so the opposite procedure applied to the pointwise product of the retained forward outputs, scaled by $M$, equals $\mathcal M_r(f,g)$.

quote.quote: To check normalization, expansion of the finite sums gives \[ F_{\boldsymbol t}^-(f*g) =M(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-f)(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-g). \] As $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+F_{\boldsymbol t}^-=I/M$, it follows that \[ M F_{\boldsymbol t}^+ \left(\frac{(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-f) (F_{\boldsymbol t}^-g)}r\right) =\frac{f*g}{rM}. \] Let $P(u,v)$ denote the exact pointwise product $uv/r$, and put $\mathcal T_+=F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$. Since $LB$ permutes records and leaves their polynomial suffixes intact, $P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v)$. Thus $\mathcal T_+$ applied to the pointwise product of the exact stored forward outputs equals $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+P(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-f,F_{\boldsymbol t}^-g)$. The displayed normalization identity identifies its exact scaling by $M$ with $\mathcal M_r(f,g)$.

children.claim: With $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ and $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$, bilinearity and the disk bounds give $\|P(\widetilde u,\widetilde v)-P(u,v)\|_\infty<2\delta$, the product truncation adds $\eta$, the contraction $\mathcal T_+$ adds its own $\delta$, and the final exact multiplication by $M$ gives error less than $M(3\delta+\eta)=\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$; if one operand has norm at most $\rho$ the returned norm is below $\rho+(1-\rho)=1$.

quote.quote: If $\widetilde h$ is the returned opposite output, its approximation bound applies to $\widetilde z$. Since $\mathcal T_+$ is a contraction, \[ \|\widetilde h-\mathcal T_+ z_*\|_\infty \leq\|\widetilde h-\mathcal T_+\widetilde z\|_\infty +\|\mathcal T_+(\widetilde z-z_*)\|_\infty <3\delta+\eta. \] The final exact multiplication by $M$ therefore gives error less than $M(3\delta+\eta)=\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$, as claimed. If one original operand has norm at most $\rho$, then $\|\mathcal M_r(f,g)\|_\infty\leq\rho$. Under the stated error margin, the returned norm is less than $\rho+(1-\rho)=1$.

children.salient: The three transforms of the convolution all keep the same bit-reversed layout order, so the only movement between them is none at all; the stored order is consumed, not corrected.

quote.quote: Now set $A=\mathsf S'$ and $B_0=\mathsf D'\mathsf J'C$. Because $\|C\|=1$, both are contractions. quote.quote: For a unit $c$ modulo $q$, let $(R_cz)_j=z_{cj}$. Substituting $h=ck$ in the Fourier sum gives \[ (F_q^+R_cz)_j =\frac1q\sum_{h=0}^{q-1}z_h e^{2\pi i h c^{-1}j/q} =(R_c^{-1}F_q^+z)_j. \] Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$, so tensoring this identity gives $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=R^{-1}F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ and hence $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$. Also $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\mathbin{\cdot}(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v) =R(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\mathbin{\cdot}F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$, because a coordinate permutation commutes with pointwise products. quote.quote: The comparison constants can be fixed for every input length at once. For sufficiently large $b$, the bounds on $n,T$ give $b/2\leq\log_2T\leq b$. quote.quote: Agarwal and Cooley used the Chinese remainder theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic convolution~\cite{AgarwalCooley1977}.
