children.claim: After the input conversion in $O(Tp)$, the algorithm performs: apply $\Phi$ with its padded layout to obtain source arrays $u,v$ of norm below $1/4$; compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}(u)$ and $\widetilde{\mathscr F}(v)$; multiply corresponding coefficients exactly and truncate to $z$; compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^+(z)$ and scale its numerators by $S$ to get $\widetilde w$; scale by $2^{2b+4}S$, round the real values to nearest integers written in $(3b+1)$-bit words and apply $\Phi^{-1}$ with padding removal; propagate radix-$2^b$ carries and output exactly $2n$ bits.

quote.quote: With these streams prepared, perform the following operations. \begin{enumerate} \item Apply the coefficient-address map $\Phi$, with its padded layout, to obtain source arrays $u,v$. Their coefficients are exact $p$-bit grid values of norm less than $1/4$. \item Compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}(u)$ and $\widetilde{\mathscr F}(v)$. \item Multiply corresponding complex coefficients exactly and truncate each real and imaginary part toward zero to $p$ fractional bits, writing the result in the common $w_{\rm c}$-bit component format. Denote the resulting source array by $z$. \item Compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)$ and multiply its grid numerators exactly by $S$, retaining the denominator $2^p$ and writing each component in signed width $w_{\rm c}+b$. Denote the represented dyadic array by $\widetilde w$. \item Multiply the grid numerators of $\widetilde w$ exactly by $2^{2b+4}S$, again retaining the denominator $2^p$, and write each component in signed width $w_{\rm c}+4b+4$. Round the represented real values to the nearest integers. At each valid address, write the rounded coefficient in one signed $(3b+1)$-bit word, most significant bit first; at every padded address, write a zero word of that width. Supply this local payload width to $\Phi^{-1}$ and apply it, including removal of the address padding, to restore the ordinary coefficient order. \item Propagate radix-$2^b$ carries in increasing coefficient order. Write the resulting bits from least to most significant on a work tape, then reverse that stream and output exactly $2n$ bits in most-significant-first order. \end{enumerate}

children.claim: Every call receives a disk-grid input within its margin; the computed first scaled result $\widetilde w$ approximates $w=(u*v)/S$ with error below $E_w2^{-p}$ where $E_w<28\cdot2^\gamma T^2L$, $L=\log_2T$; and after the second scale the absolute error is $2^{2b+4}S\cdot28\cdot2^\gamma T^2L\cdot2^{-6b}<448b\,2^{-3b/4}<1/2$, so rounding gives the unique correct integer coefficients in $[0,2^{3b})$ and carry propagation yields the exact $2n$-bit product.
children.method: Propagate errors through linear and bilinear contractions, adding at each stage: ring convolution $E_{\rm ring}<5TL$, complex convolution $6TL$, chirp transform $8TL$, source transform $E_s=9\cdot2^\gamma TL$; combine the two forward errors, the product truncation and the opposite transform; multiply by the exact scales $S$ and $2^{2b+4}S$ and compare with $1/2$ using $S\le T<2^b$, $L<b$ and $\gamma\le b/4$; propagate carries with the invariant on partial sums.

motivation.text: Every map in the pipeline is a linear or bilinear contraction in the sup norm, so errors add rather than multiply, and the digit scale $2^{-b-2}$ with precision $p=6b$ leaves a factor $2^{-6b}$ against scales whose product is about $2^{5b}$ times a polynomial in $b$.

quote.quote: A linear contraction propagates an input error without increasing it. For a bilinear contraction $\mathcal M$, replacing its operands gives \[ \|\mathcal M(f',g')-\mathcal M(f,g)\| \le \|f'-f\|\,\|g'\|+\|f\|\,\|g'-g\|. \] When all four operands are in the disk, their two errors therefore add.

children.claim: For the ring convolution the three transform errors and the polynomial-product truncation total less than $3L+2$ before the scale $M$, so the returned error is bounded by $E_{\rm ring}=M(3L+2)<5TL$; if one operand has norm at most $.7$, bilinear contraction gives $\|\mathcal M_r(f,g)\|\le.7$ and the computed output has norm below $.7+5TLh_p<.701$, the disk margin after the scale without clipping.

quote.quote: Before that multiplication, the three transform errors and the polynomial-product truncation total less than $3L+2$. Thus the error of the returned normalized convolution is bounded by \[ E_{\rm ring}:=M(3L+2)<5TL. \] If one operand has norm at most $.7$, bilinear contraction gives $\|\mathcal M_r(f,g)\|\le.7$. Its computed grid output consequently has norm less than $.7+5TLh_p<.701$ for large $n$. This proves the disk margin after the scale $M$, without clipping the output.

children.claim: Inserting the exact normalized $\mathcal M_r$ at the twisted inputs $\iota f'$ and $\iota g'$, its bilinear contraction propagates the two twist errors (each below $4$), its approximation contributes $E_{\rm ring}$ and the output untwist below $4$, so $\|\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(f,g)-\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g)\|<(E_{\rm ring}+12)h_p<6TLh_p$.

quote.quote: To compare it with $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g)$, insert the exact normalized $\mathcal M_r$ at $\iota f'$ and $\iota g'$. Its bilinear contraction bound propagates the two input twist errors, each less than $4$. Its approximation contributes $E_{\rm ring}$, and the output untwist contributes less than $4$. All these comparisons are at the normalized $\mathcal M_r$ interface, after its factor $M$. They give \[ \|\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(f,g) -\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g)\| <(E_{\rm ring}+4+4+4)h_p<6TLh_p.

children.claim: For $\|x\|\le.6$ the chirp data operand $x_0$ has norm at most $.6$ and the outputs have norm below $.701$; inserting the exact bilinear $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}$, the kernel approximation contributes less than $2$, each endpoint phase less than $4$ and the convolution less than $6TL$, so $\|\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)-QF_{\boldsymbol t}x\|<(6TL+10)h_p<8TLh_p$.

quote.quote: For its error, the exact operands $a$ and $\overline a\cdot x$ are in the disk because every entry of $a$ has modulus one. The kernel approximation contributes less than $2$ and the first endpoint multiplication contributes less than $4$ when inserted into the exact bilinear contraction $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}$. The computed convolution contributes less than $6TL$, and the last endpoint multiplication less than $4$. Equation~\eqref{eq:permuted-chirp} identifies the exact result, so \[ \|\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)-QF_{\boldsymbol t}x\| <(6TL+2+4+4)h_p<8TLh_p.

children.claim: For a source input of norm at most $.5$, the expansion has error below $dp^2$ and norm below $.51$, the chirp output is in the disk, and inserting the exact contractions $\mathcal A$, $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$, $\mathcal B_0$ the error before the scale is below $2dp^2+8TL$; multiplying by $2^\gamma$ gives error below $E_sh_p$ with $E_s=9\cdot2^\gamma TL$ since $2dp^2<TL$ eventually, the scaled output has norm at most $.501$, and conjugation gives the same for the opposite procedure.

quote.quote: Insert the exact contractions $\mathcal A$, $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$, and $\mathcal B_0$ at the computed inputs. The error before the source scale is less than $2dp^2+8TL$. Multiplication by $2^\gamma$ therefore gives error less than $2^\gamma(2dp^2+8TL)h_p$, which is bounded by $E_sh_p$ with \begin{equation}\label{eq:source-error} E_s=9\,2^\gamma TL, \end{equation} because $2dp^2<TL$ eventually. The exact source transform $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$ is a contraction, so the scaled approximation has norm at most $.5+E_sh_p<.501$. Its exact numerator scaling therefore also leaves a disk-grid output without clipping. Conjugation preserves the grid and norm, so the opposite procedure has the same error and disk guarantee.

children.claim: With $U=RF_{\boldsymbol s}u$, $V_1=RF_{\boldsymbol s}v$ of norm below $1/4$ and computed versions of norm below $.26$, $z=Q_p(\widetilde U\cdot\widetilde V_1)$ has norm below $.5$ and error $(2E_s+2)h_p$; with $G=RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ and $G(U\cdot V_1)=(u*v)/S^2$, inserting $G$ at $z$ gives $\|\widetilde{\mathscr F}^+(z)-G(U\cdot V_1)\|<(3E_s+2)h_p$, so the first scale by $S$ gives $\widetilde w$ with error $E_w=S(3E_s+2)<28\cdot2^\gamma T^2L$ and norm below $1/16+10^{-3}<1$.

quote.quote: The first exact numerator multiplication by $S$ gives $\widetilde w$, approximating $w=(u*v)/S$ with error less than $E_wh_p$, where \[ E_w:=S(3E_s+2)<28\,2^\gamma T^2L. \] Each coefficient of $w$ is an average of $S$ products of coefficients of $u$ and $v$, so $\|w\|<1/16$. The earlier cutoff therefore gives \[ \|\widetilde w\|<1/16+E_wh_p<1/16+10^{-3}<1. \] This proves the disk bound for the computed first scaled result.

children.claim: Since $S\le T<2^b$ and $L<b$ eventually, the final absolute error after the second scale is $2^{2b+4}S\cdot28\cdot2^\gamma T^2L\cdot2^{-6b}<448b\,2^{-b+\gamma}\le448b\,2^{-3b/4}<1/2$; the true coefficients are integers, so the nearest integer to the represented value $H_j/2^p$ is the unique correct coefficient, which lies in $[0,2^{3b})$.

quote.quote: In tensor order, the unscaled integer coefficient array is $2^{2b+4}S w$. This second occurrence of $S$ reverses the normalization still present in $w$, and $2^{2b+4}$ reverses the two input scales. Both multiplications act exactly on grid numerators. Since $S\le T<2^b$ and $L<b$ eventually, the final absolute error is less than \begin{equation}\label{eq:final-error} 2^{2b+4}S\cdot28\,2^\gamma T^2L\cdot2^{-6b} <448b\,2^{-b+\gamma} \le448b\,2^{-3b/4}<\frac12. \end{equation} The true coefficients are real integers. If $H_j$ is the real numerator after the second scaling, its represented value is $H_j/2^p$. The strict error below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to that value the unique correct coefficient.

children.claim: With $Q_0=2^b$ the carry recurrence $d_j=(c_j+k_j)\bmod Q_0$, $k_{j+1}=\lfloor(c_j+k_j)/Q_0\rfloor$ keeps $0\le k_j\le q(Q_0-1)<Q_0^2$ and maintains the invariant $\sum_{h<j}c_hQ_0^h=\sum_{h<j}d_hQ_0^h+k_jQ_0^j$, which fixes the first $j$ radix digits of the product; the exact product is below $2^{2n}$, so exactly $2n$ bits are output after one reversal of the digit stream.

quote.quote: The defining relation $c_j+k_j=d_j+Q_0k_{j+1}$ also gives the exact invariant \[ \sum_{h<j}c_hQ_0^h =\sum_{h<j}d_hQ_0^h+k_jQ_0^j. \] It holds for $j=0$, and the defining relation proves its next instance. The unprocessed terms are multiples of $Q_0^j$, so the identity fixes the first $j$ radix digits of the full product. The value $k_j$ is the carry from the processed coefficients into the remaining positions. After $\Phi^{-1}$ the coefficients occur in increasing ordinary index, so this carry scan proceeds from least to most significant. Carry storage and work per coefficient are $O(b)$ bits and steps. Write each digit's bits from low to high on a work tape, and drain the final $O(b)$-bit carry in the same order. Copy the completed stream backward once to obtain most-significant-first order. The stream has length $O(Sb)=O(Tp)$, including chunk padding and the final carry, so this reversal is a charged linear tape pass. The exact product is less than $2^{2n}$; all bits above position $2n-1$ are therefore zero. Remove only those zero padding bits and retain leading zeros as needed to produce exactly $2n$ bits. Zero inputs obey the same invariant and output rule.

children.salient: All the accumulated error, through roughly $\ell+2$ transform rounds, Gaussian maps and chirps on $\Theta(n)$ values, stays below $1/2$ with a precision of only $p=6b$ bits, six times the digit width, because every stage is a contraction and errors add linearly.

children.claim: With $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$, every operation's cost divided by $V$ is bounded by one of the powers $p^{\epsilon(1+c)}$, $p^{1-\epsilon c(1-\tau)}$, $p^{1-\epsilon(1-\lambda')}$, $p^{\tau+\epsilon(2-\tau)}$, $p^{3/4+\delta+3\epsilon/2}$, $p^{\epsilon+\delta}$, $p^{1-\epsilon}$, whose margins below one are all at least $2^{-181}=2\kappa$, so the total time is $O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$ for large $n$, and schoolbook multiplication below one cutoff gives one machine with worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ for every $n$.
children.method: Tabulate the normalized costs of prefix-slot moves, layout chunk exchanges, simultaneous rounds, CRT and axis layouts, Gaussian line maps, chirps and twists, packed polynomial products, scaling and carries; compute the seven margins from the fixed rational exponents; absorb setup, descriptor and exceptional-stream work as $o(V)$.

motivation.text: All work is organized as passes over arrays of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits, so the natural unit is cost per stored bit, and the theorem follows once every normalized cost is a power of $p=\Theta(\log n)$ strictly below one; the smallest margin, from the chunk-exchange term, determines $\kappa$.

children.claim: The seven dominant normalized powers have margins $g_1=1-\epsilon(1+c)$, $g_2=\epsilon c(1-\tau)$, $g_3=\epsilon(1-\lambda')$, $g_4=1-\tau-\epsilon(2-\tau)$, $g_5=1/4-\delta-3\epsilon/2$, $g_6=1-\delta-\epsilon$, $g_7=\epsilon$, and direct substitution gives $g_1>1/2$, $g_2=2^{-181}$, $g_3=2^{-129}$, $g_4>2^{-51}$, $g_5>1/8$, $g_6>1/2$, $g_7=2^{-75}$, so $\min_ig_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

quote.quote: Direct substitution gives \[ g_1>\frac12,\quad g_2=2^{-181},\quad g_3=2^{-129},\quad g_4>2^{-51},\quad g_5>\frac18,\quad g_6>\frac12,\quad g_7=2^{-75}. \] Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$. This explicit slack will cover any remaining fixed power of $\log p$.

children.claim: The transform layout uses $O(p/K)$ exchanges of width-$K$ chunks because $d\ell=O(p)$, each costing $O(VK^\tau)$, so its normalized total is $O(pK^{\tau-1})$; each of the at most $\ell$ simultaneous rounds costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ including basis changes, deterministic repair, row padding and cleanup.

quote.quote: Its positional layout uses $O(p/K)$ exchanges of width-$K$ chunks, because $d\ell=O(p)$. Each exchange costs $O(VK^\tau)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:chunk-swap}, so the normalized total is \[ O(p/K)\,K^\tau=O(pK^{\tau-1}). \] For the at most $\ell$ simultaneous rounds, Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} supplies $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ per round. Its bound already includes the binary basis changes, deterministic repair, row padding and removal, all base-$m$ groups, and fixed-tape cleanup.

children.claim: Setup at the at most $p^A$ recursion visits costs $p^{A+C}=o(Tp)$, per-record descriptor work costs $O(Tp^{A+C}/r)=o(Tp)$, per-line setup $O(dTp^C/r)=o(Tp)$, and the compact exceptional-stream sorting over all packed calls costs $O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V)$, since $r$ exceeds every fixed power of $p$, $d=O(p^\epsilon)$ and $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$; this is a deterministic worst-case bound.

quote.quote: Since there are at most $p^A$ visits, each of volume $O(V)$, the compact sorting costs sum to at most \[ O\!\left(dp2^{-K}\sum_{\rm calls}V_{\rm call}\right) =O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V) \] for another fixed exponent $A'$. Here $d=O(p^\epsilon)$ and $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ with $\epsilon c>0$. Predicate and key arithmetic is the polynomial work per record counted above. This is a deterministic worst-case bound.

children.claim: Each displayed power is at most $1-2\kappa$ and any fixed power of $\log p$ is at most $p^\kappa$ eventually, so the large-input bound is $O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$; fixing one cutoff beyond all size, precision, margin and layout conditions and using schoolbook multiplication below it gives a single deterministic fixed-tape machine with worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ for every input length, producing the required $2n$-bit product.

quote.quote: Each of the seven displayed powers is at most $1-2\kappa$ by \eqref{eq:margin-list}. Any fixed power of $\log p$ is at most $p^\kappa$ eventually. The complete large-input bound is consequently \[ O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}). \] Fix one cutoff beyond all the size, precision, margin and layout conditions, and use schoolbook multiplication below it. The finitely many smaller lengths are included by enlarging the implicit constant. With $\lg n=\max\{\lceil\log_2n\rceil,1\}$, the resulting single fixed-alphabet, fixed-tape deterministic machine has worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ for every input length and produces precisely the required $2n$-bit product.

children.salient: The binding term is the layout chunk exchange $pK^{\tau-1}$ with margin $\epsilon c(1-\tau)=2^{-181}$; every other term has a far larger margin, and $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is half the smallest margin, the other half absorbing all logarithmic factors.
